content_units: Best-Fit Laptop Snapshot
Your priorities are   value  ,   battery life  , and   4-year longevity  , with hard preferences for   14-inch or smaller  ,   16GB+ RAM  , and   under 1.5 kg  .
Based on those criteria,   Option A is the best overall pick  , with   Option B as the best value-oriented alternative  .
Ranked Laptop Comparison
Rank   Option   Price   Size   RAM / SSD   Battery   Weight   Fit vs your needs   Verdict
1     A       USD 1,249     13.6"   16GB / 512GB     18 hours       1.24 kg     Meets all preferences strongly     Best overall
2     B       USD 1,199     14"   16GB / 1TB   10 hours   1.47 kg   Meets all stated requirements     Best value
3     C     USD 1,279   14"     32GB / 512GB     8 hours     1.52 kg     Misses weight preference   Strong spec pick, weaker fit
4     D     USD 999   13.3"     8GB   / 512GB   17 hours   1.2 kg   Misses minimum RAM target   Not recommended for 4 years
Option 1:   A — Best overall balance     Long battery life, light weight, and enough memory for grad school + light analysis over 4 years     Strongest all-around fit
Option 2:   B — Best value buy     Lowest price among the qualifying options and 1TB storage is excellent for files/datasets     Best price-to-storage value
Option 3:   C — Performance-leaning trade-off     32GB RAM is great for heavier multitasking, but battery and weight are weaker     Best RAM, worse portability
Option 4:   D — Budget-friendly but short-lived     Great portability and battery, but 8GB RAM is the main limitation     Least future-proof
4-Year Use Recommendation
Recommended: Option A
Why A wins:
-   Battery life is the standout  : 18 hours gives the most flexibility for classes, library work, travel, and long days away from outlets.
-   Portable enough for daily carry  : 1.24 kg is comfortably under your limit.
-   Meets the memory floor  : 16GB is the right baseline for graduate school and light data analysis over 4 years.
-   Still within budget  : It stays under your USD 1,300 ceiling while maximizing everyday usability.
Why it beats B:
- B is cheaper by only   USD 50  , but A gives a much larger battery advantage and lower weight.
- For a 4-year device, that battery/portability gain is likely worth more than the extra 512GB of storage for most students.
Why it beats C:
- C has excellent   32GB RAM  , but it is   over your preferred weight limit   and has clearly weaker battery life.
- Unless your “light data analysis” may grow into heavier local workloads, the extra RAM is probably not worth the portability trade-off.
Why D falls behind:
-   8GB RAM   is the biggest risk for longevity.
- It may feel fine now for basic tasks, but over 4 years with heavier browser use, research apps, Zoom, and analysis tools, it is the least future-proof.
Buying Logic for Your Priorities
If you want the safest long-term choice
Pick   A  .
- Best combination of   battery + portability + adequate RAM
- Most likely to stay pleasant to use through graduate school
If you want the smartest money-saving choice
Pick   B  .
- Saves   USD 50
- Adds   1TB storage
- Good if you care more about local file space than all-day battery
If your data analysis may become heavier than “light”
Pick   C   only as a deliberate trade-off.
- 32GB RAM is excellent for larger datasets, multiple tools, and heavier multitasking
- But it fails your preferred weight threshold and has the shortest battery life here
Context Used for Ranking
I treated your priorities in this order:
1.   Value
2.   Battery life
3.   Longevity over 4 years
I also treated these as important fit constraints:
-   14-inch or smaller
-   16GB RAM minimum
-   Under 1.5 kg preferred
Because of that,   D was heavily penalized for 8GB RAM  , and   C was penalized for exceeding your weight preference  .
